aliases: Fly's Eye I and II site

coordinates.note: This is a region marker (kind campus is the closest allowed approximate kind), not a campus. Only a degree-level position is given by the sources read ("40deg N, 113 deg W"; Bird et al. 1998 say "(40 o North)"). The point is therefore a region marker for the Dugway Proving Ground, not a survey position: it is roughly 25 km from the HiRes sites, and Fly's Eye I and II themselves stood 3.4 km apart. No source read gives the Fly's Eye I or II coordinates; listed under unresolved.
coordinates.quote: The Fly’s Eye experiment was located at Dugway, Utah (40deg N, 113 deg W)

name: Fly's Eye site, Dugway Proving Ground (approximate)
notes: Approximate region marker; see the coordinate note. Fly's Eye I and Fly's Eye II (3.4 km apart) are not separately located.

summary.plain: The Utah desert area on the Dugway Proving Ground where the original Fly's Eye cosmic-ray detector stood in the 1980s and early 1990s.
summary.technical: Approximate marker for the two original Fly's Eye stations (Fly's Eye I with 67 mirrors; Fly's Eye II, 3.4 km away) on the Dugway Proving Ground; the position is only known to about a degree from the sources read.
